title: Ops Anchor proxy for multi-runbook rehearsal and safe admin utility execution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Support engineers rely on many small admin utilities and ad-hoc runbooks stored across docs and snippets. Running these in production is error-prone: inconsistent environment loading, missing idempotency, and limited observability. We also lack a safe, repeatable rehearsal environment to validate runbooks before they touch live state.

Proposal: Implement an "Anchor" proxy service (Anchorlet) that intercepts invoked admin utilities/runbook steps and routes them through a rehearsal/execution pipeline. Anchorlet responsibilities:
- Provide a canonical invocation API for runbook steps (typed inputs, metadata, caller, correlation id).
- Validate inputs and apply idempotency checks and dry-run toggles.
- Rehearse side-effecting steps in an isolated sandbox (prefix-mock resources / replay harness) and produce deterministic diff reports.
- Optionally escalate to live execution with an enforced approval and audit trail.
- Emit structured telemetry compatible with Console rollouts and Optimize tooling so we can attribute cost/latency to individual steps.

Why this is different: Instead of wrapping runbooks ad-hoc, Anchorlet centralizes safety, telemetry, and rehearsals while preserving developer ergonomics (shortflows / snippets can be registered as anchorlets). It focuses on runbooks-as-tasks: every runbook step becomes a first-class, reviewable, and replayable unit.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We will not attempt to run full production-scale replay of long-running remediation flows in Cycle 1; scope limited to discrete admin utilities and shortflows (<30s).
- Sandbox model uses namespaced test resources and prefix-mockers for cloud calls. This is cheaper than full infra snapshots but requires careful coverage lists to ensure safety.
- We prefer syntactic registration (manifest + contract) over heavy reflection to avoid startup overhead.
- Security review is required because Anchorlet can escalate to live effects; plan to integrate with RBAC service and KMS gating.

Telemetry and observability goals:
- Per-step latency, tokenization cost (for any LLM-driven steps), success/failure counts, and replay-dryrun diffs.
- Dashboards: per-shortflow heatmap, dangerous-step alerts, and runbook regression alerts integrated with Console.

Deliverables for Cycle 2026-W11:
- Anchorlet HTTP API + registration manifest schema (openapi draft).
- Rehearsal runner with mock adapter for S3 and service-config mutations.
- Basic Console panel prototype showing per-step telemetry.
- E2E demo: register 3 canonical shortflows, run dry-run, show diff, and perform gated live execute.

Risks / mitigations:
- False sense of safety if mocks diverge from prod APIs — mitigate with canary live checks and guidance to authors.
- Permission escalation abuse — mitigate with RBAC enforced on escalation and signed approvals.
- Telemetry noise — limit sampling initially and refine metrics schema.
acceptance_criteria: Anchorlet exposes OpenAPI endpoints for registering and invoking runbook steps
Rehearsal runner can execute registered shortflows in dry-run mode and produce a structured diff report
RBAC gating prevents live escalation without approval from required roles
Console panel shows per-step latency and success/failure rates for anchored runbooks
At least 3 internal shortflows are migrated and rehearsed with explanatory docs and a recorded demo
